commonFiniteFixture.freshClientRepeat: All ten new projection reads repeat after each earlier client is fully closed. This is client reopen, not engine restart.
commonFiniteFixture.sameTimeCapture: Pause a legitimately internal source-P acquisition after it returns P1, commit P2 at the same recorded instant through a second normal writer, then resume the helper. Verify returned P1 plus old value/no future retirement. New fresh invocation captures P2 and returns new value.
commonFiniteFixture.rawCompatibilityControls: Read ordinary raw history and old-R match before/after new reads. Preserve all complete original lifetime fields and verify no new source fact, claim or operation receipt was created by a read.

A.hypothesis: A narrowly named SDK helper over the existing closed native assertion relations can expose truthful known-at-cut assertion metadata without changing the default Triplex runtime or raw lifetime readers.
A.seam: New isolated XTDB helper/application package using current makeXtdbNativeQueries. Native provider acquires P exactly once. Use ctx.facts() for live-at-valid, and ctx.history() plus the SAME explicit V predicate for known-at-valid. Add only declared selective QueryRequest predicates; no Datalog lowering or arbitrary load-query fallback.
A.projection: Map bounded declared native assertion columns into the distinct result type. Existing Native/Sources SQL CASE/XTQL conditional hides future retirement fields inside the qualified read surface. The test harness must compare raw actual results, not apply this mapping for the product.
A.cost: One existing source-cut lookup plus one bounded answer query, decoding only final selected assertions. No new data copy/index/materialized relation or source writes. maxRows+1 refusal, timeout/cancellation and trace work remain charged.
A.initialScope: Committed database assertions only; no transaction pending overlay is serialized or merged. Calling this separate provider from a transaction does not make pending facts committed. No promise of portable implementation before sibling qualification.

B.hypothesis: A separate basis-aware adapter assertion-read primitive can provide the same result/cut contract while retaining ordinary raw reads and transaction/write behavior.
B.seam: An isolated opt-in snapshot read entry acquires P with currentCommitPosition once outside any active write callback and passes P only through ResolvedTemporalBasis to a NEW private adapter projection. Existing query/getById/retract/history remain untouched; no global runtime metadata default is changed.
B.projection: Use the same known-retirement test as Native/Sources for three backend SELECT CASE columns; preserve raw row filters/value decoding. In known-at-valid mode apply V explicitly even though current history() is all-business-time. Decode into the same distinct SnapshotAssertion result.
B.cost: One cut read plus one bounded selective assertion query; three scalar projections per returned row. A narrow new internal adapter/read SPI and a separate SDK entry are required, followed by Core/public-DTS/package tests. No persistent copy or write is required.
B.initialScope: Committed-only read entry; explicitly refuse/keep outside active pending transactions in the first candidate. Pending/child/retry semantics are not inferred from raw getById. A later pending-aware version needs an explicit authority for sourceK plus pending state and its own tests.

C.reason: Engine system time/snapshot tokens are different coordinates from the deterministic numeric Triplex R/V and scope P. Current submit returns only await visibility token; it records no authoritative logical-P to engine-snapshot map. Multiple staged logical positions may share one physical commit, so even a mapping may not replace logical predicates/projection.
C.prerequisite: Demonstrate exact same-scope operation/commit/snapshot mapping, atomicity, same-timestamp and multi-logical-position cases, reconnect/unknown ACK/retention. No R==engine-system-time conversion, latest SHOW after COMMIT shortcut, or using CLOCK_TIME as historical authority.
